The narrating participant reports Richard seeing “me” and describes “my” emotional response.
Sustained autobiographical narration recounts Honor's childhood memory through repeated “I” and “my.”

person_note: The event passages repeatedly expose Honor Harris as a participating “I” narrator across childhood memories, her relationship with Richard, and her later reflections. The two dialogue-bucket quotations marked first are diagnostic only because their external speech beats say “I asked” or “I answered”; the spoken pronouns themselves are not being used. Gnomic “we,” direct address, and the memorial inscription are non-base material. Whole-book scholarly evidence explicitly identifies Honor's narration as first person, while the estate-approved author site independently describes the story as her retrospective self-narration. No source indicated a sustained third- or second-person section; the only material uncertainty is the limited availability of an authorized continuous excerpt, which is offset by the consistent quote evidence and whole-book scholarly analysis.
